title: candidate-feedback-draft-daniel-park-2026-03-07
summary: Strong backend systems engineer with solid low-level understanding of memory/KV cache tradeoffs. Good ownership instincts and practical tradeoff reasoning. Missed on a couple of edge cases in async debugging exercise but recovered well. Overall leaning +1 (hire) for senior role, recommend manager-level calibration for L4 vs L5.
strengths:
- Deep understanding of caching and KV eviction strategies; referenced concrete latency/cost tradeoffs from past work.
- Clear communicator when mapping problem to constraints (latency SLOs, memory caps).
- Experience shipping production inference features (worked on batching and online cache warmup).
- Passion for observability: suggested useful signal ideas (per-token latency percentiles, KV hit heatmaps).
weaknesses:
- Struggled initially with async traceback debugging; needed hints to reason about event loop vs thread pools.
- Some unfamiliarity with our exact compilation/kernel-selection heuristics; aware at high level but lacked depth.
- Limited exposure to ML model formats (mostly worked on TF-serving and custom protobufs).
scorecard: Technical (data structures/algorithms): 4 - good problem solving, clean code, missed a micro-optimization but fine for role
Systems Design: 4 - solid tradeoffs, thought about cost/latency, could expand on cross-region failure modes
Debugging/Tooling: 3 - handles common cases, needs work on async/concurrency edge cases
Ownership & Execution: 5 - clear examples of driving features to production, shipped monitoring + rollback plans
Communication & Collaboration: 4 - concise, good at surfacing assumptions, engages well
recommendation: Recommend hire (senior), pending manager calibration on level. Strong fit for runtime perf team; could ramp quickly into batching/caching work.
next_steps:
- Share with hiring committee (HIRE-1234).
- Run quick follow-up on async concurrency question (15-20m with Priya) to validate edge-case coverage.
- Reference check focusing on ownership of perf features.
- Compensation banding: start L4 comp discussion; consider L5 if follow-up demonstrates broader system architecture experience.
notes_to_self: Remember to add example snippets Daniel mentioned (LRU-with-prefetch) to our interview bank. Could adapt his observability suggestions into a take-home prompt. Also flag for Kate (hiring manager) that he has strong product empathy.
raw_interview_log:
(scratch) - 09:00 intro, background on serving runtime at previous company (built caching layer for speech inference).
- Coding: streaming window sum problem (used deque solution, O(n) time) - asked about amortized cost and memory; good answers.
- Design: design a KV cache with async prefetch for hot keys - proposed background prefetchers, backpressure, TTLs; didn't fully address thundering herd but suggested circuit-breaker.
- Deep dive: described real incident where quantization change increased latency due to kernel selection mismatch - good postmortem thinking.
- Culture/behavior: wants to work on product-facing infra, mentions OK with on-call rotations.
